scope: Narrow parser corrections, pending root integration and independent source review.
implementation_constraints: Translator selection uses the exact legacy patterns and qualifying-name behavior. The Unicode name parser starts at that same selected source position; it never selects an earlier newly recognized credit.
Entirely missing translator credits remain unchanged for separate scope review.
Sentence boundaries, initials, attested abbreviated name parts, combining marks, apostrophes and wiki markup have targeted tests.
The added languages are fallback values only when no previously recognized category language exists. Multilingual page 2476 remains German under the existing compatibility choice.
Only prefixed p./pp. candidates with explicit reference/annotation/note labels or noncontiguous numeric lists are rejected as book extents.
Explicit number-before-unit extents, N/(M)p. numbered/unnumbered notation and standalone pp. N remain supported.
No publisher, location, edition-selection, general language-inference or scope model was changed.
A proposed name boundary at a period followed by an initial is quarantined by retaining the legacy value; no page-ID exceptions are used.

source_review.page_count: Inspected all 95 changed locator snippets. Each removed scalar is documented as a citation/reference/annotation/illustration locator or noncontiguous page list. The patch does not claim that all remaining prefixed p./pp. cases are valid extents.
source_review.translator: Each change has both old and new exact selected source spans and the complete unchanged stage-02 source. All changed names retain the legacy-selected occurrence. New values are literal source substrings; 202 repair Unicode truncation, 330 terminate trailing prose, and four retain a final initial's period.
source_review.language: All 57 changes fill previously empty category-language values with the exact source category language. There are no existing scalar switches.

known_remaining_limits: The translator selector still cannot resolve author/edition/contribution scope. Preservation of a legacy anchor prevents a new occurrence-selection policy but does not ratify the old flat choice.
Unsupported entirely missing translator credits and expanded-name brackets are intentionally unchanged.
Unlabelled single p./pp. locators can still be accepted by the legacy prefix rule. A blanket rejection would need a broader source review and policy for prefixed volume extents.
Book extent extraction still applies the existing pattern precedence across multiple publications. This package does not select a universally correct edition.
Language remains category-derived; explicit body labels such as Chechen and contextual German inference on page 72 are outside this patch.
